dataset: HMRC tax receipts and National Insurance contributions for the UK
caveats: Cash receipts are when money reaches HMRC, which differs from accrued revenue in HMRC's annual accounts.
Columns include totals and their components (for example Income Tax and PAYE Income Tax); do not add columns together.
[x] in the source (not available or not applicable) is stored as null, not zero. Negative values are repayments and are kept.
Recent months are provisional and are revised in later releases.
notes: Receipts Notes
Total Paid Over. Comprises of payments into the Consolidated Fund and all payovers of NICs excluding those of Northern Ireland. This dataset is published monthly by the ONS in table PSA7D.
Total HMRC Receipts. Includes payable tax credits, and all payments into the Consolidated Fund and all payovers of NICs including those of Northern Ireland.

Income Tax. Figures are gross of personal tax credits and includes Pay As You Earn and Self-Assessment income tax (also shown separately in the table) as well as other smaller elements of income tax such as repayments.

Income Tax. From August 2026, HMRC introduced monthly alignment of Income Tax receipts to HMRC accounting data, applied retrospectively to receipts from April 2026 onwards. As this is the first year of implementation, direct year-on-year comparisons, including year-to-date comparisons, should be interpreted with caution, as receipts from April 2026 onwards reflect the new monthly alignment approach.

NICs. Total NICs includes Class 1, 1A, 2 and 4, Class 1B, Class 3, recoveries of statutory payments, and various classes of NICs paid via the NIC Office or following an investigation settlement. Receipts are gross of provisional estimates for statutory payments and are subject to revision.

NICs. From August 2026, HMRC introduced monthly alignment of NICs to HMRC accounting data, applied retrospectively to receipts from April 2026 onwards. As this is the first year of implementation, direct year-on-year comparisons, including year-to-date comparisons, should be interpreted with caution, as receipts from April 2026 onwards reflect the new monthly alignment approach.

PAYE NIC1 & SA NIC2&4. From April 2015, the additional columns for NICs have been populated where the underpinning data are readily available for the full tax-year. PAYE NICs (Employer) includes class 1 NICs paid by employers and class 1A NICs, and excludes NIC1B receipts, which are paid as part of a PAYE settlement agreement.

VAT. From August 2026, HMRC introduced monthly alignment of VAT receipts to HMRC accounting data, applied retrospectively to receipts from April 2026 onwards. As this is the first year of implementation, direct year-on-year comparisons, including year-to-date comparisons, should be interpreted with caution, as receipts from April 2026 onwards reflect the new monthly alignment approach.

Corporation Tax (CT). Receipts are gross of provisional tax credits and are subject to change, due to a lag in return data becoming available for analysis: this publication includes updates from April 2017 onwards. Figures include offshore which are also shown seperately in the table. From July 2011 Bank Levy receipts are shown separately and from April 2016 Bank Surcharge receipts are shown separately.

Offshore CT. The majority of UK oil and gas companies' payments are due in three instalments (July, October and January). From April 2015, where the data is readily available, the receipts reporting pattern is now aligned to these peak instalment months.

Diverted Profits Tax (DPT). Figures are net DPT charges. DPT encourages companies to change contrived arrangements and pay CT on their profits in line with their economic activity. DPT may be repaid where a company makes an amendment to bring its taxable diverted profits into charge to CT: these are included under CT. The full impact of DPT legislation is available in the Transfer Pricing and Diverted Profits Tax statistics published on GOV.UK.
Digital Services Tax. Introduced on 1 April 2020 on the revenues of search engines, social media services and online marketplaces which derive value from UK users.

Residential Property Developer Tax. Introduced on 1 April 2022 and receipts are reported quarterly or six-monthly. This tax applies to the largest property developers on the profits they make from UK residential property development.
Energy Profits Levy. Introduced on 26 May 2022 on the profits of oil and gas companies. The first payments were received in December 2022.

Electricity Generator Levy. Introduced on 1 January 2023 on the exceptional receipts of electricity generators. The first payments were received in Summer 2023 and receipts are reported quarterly, six-monthly or annually.
Economic Crime Levy. Introduced on 1 April 2022 on businesses falling under anti-money laundering regulations. The first payments to HMRC were received in September 2023.
Petroleum Revenue Tax receipts from 2025-26 are published twice a year around the peak repayment months.
Inheritance Tax. Excludes non-cash elements which are published in the ONS National Accounts under code 'LSON'.
Stamps Taxes. The overall total can be calculated by including receipts from Shares, Land Tax and Annual Tax on Enveloped Dwellings.
Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT). Excludes SDLT devolved to Scotland from April 2015, and to Wales from April 2018.
Landfill tax (LFT). Excludes LFT devolved to Scotland from April 2015, and to Wales from April 2019.

Alcohol Duties. Wine and Cider outturns from April 2023 are undergoing further assurance and year-on-year comparisons for these sub-components over this period should be interpreted with caution until this assurance is complete. Total alcohol duties are unaffected.
Climate Change Levy. From April 2013, includes receipts from Carbon Price Floor.

Penalties. Penalties relate to taxes and duties only with National Insurance Contributions (NICs) penalties included in the NICs figures. Annual data is only available back to the tax year 2010 to 2011.
Expenditure Notes
Child and Working Tax Credits ended on 5 April 2025. From April 2025, any repayments or payments data will be reported annually following the publication of the Annual Reports and Accounts.
Corporation Tax Credits. Monthly data unavailable due to the lag in return data becoming available. Tax credits are provisional and annual data is subject to change to incorporate new available data.

Child Benefit from April 2011, is consistent with HMRC Resource Accounts. From March 2026 and 2025-26 onwards, March outturn will include a social benefit accrual, reflecting updated Financial Resources Advisory Board guidance to recognise backdated claims at the point of entitlement: this accrual will be reversed each April
Tax-Free Child Care. Introduced in April 2017. For further information, please see the step by step guide published on GOV.UK.
Annual Contribution by Tax
Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax and National Insurance Contributions. Receipts for the tax years 2010 to 2011, through to, 2012 to 2013, include Bank Payroll Tax.
Business taxes. Includes Corporation Tax, Petroleum Revenue Tax, Bank Levy, Bank Surcharge, Diverted Profits Tax, Digital Services Tax, and Energy Profits Levy.
Stamp Taxes. Includes Annual Tax on Enveloped Dwellings receipts from 2013.
Environmental taxes. Includes Landfill Tax (LFT), Climate Change Levy (CCL), Aggregates Levy, Carbon Price Floor (CPF) and Plastic Packaging Tax.
Other taxes. Includes Apprenticeship Levy, Betting and Gaming Duties, Insurance Premium Tax, Soft Drinks Industry Levy, Swiss Captial Tax, Customs Duties and Penalties.
End of Notes
